chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said:

A man asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) while I was listening: A man marries a woman for a fixed term (mut'ah) and stipulates upon her that he will not acknowledge her child, but she subsequently brings forth a child. Should he deny the child? He emphasized in this matter and said: He denies (paternity). And how can he deny it, out of respect for it? The man said: But I suspect her (of not being the true mother or of other issues).

He (al-Rida) said: It is not fitting for you to marry except a trustworthy (woman). Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'The fornicator marries not except a female idolator or a polytheess, and the female idolator none marries her except a fornicator or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father denying paternity of a child born from a temporary marriage (mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that a man in temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) who stipulates non-acknowledgment of offspring still bears legal paternity, as he 'denies' the child out of pride rather than legal right. He advises marrying a trustworthy (*ma'muna*) woman to minimize suspicion, linking this social prudence to the Quranic principle that fornicators marry only similar partners, thereby establishing a thematic link between marital integrity and lineage certainty. This ruling underscores the Shia view that *mut'ah* confers full paternity rights unless explicitly nullified by valid legal grounds, not merely by stipulation.
